title: Josh Jacobs Granted Full Week of Practice; Game Status Still Pending, NBC Sports Reports
body:
The Green Bay Packers confirmed that running back Josh Jacobs will be cleared for a full week of practice ahead of Sunday’s showdown with the Detroit Lions, while defensive end Micah Parsons remains sidelined. Jacobs, who was placed on the inactive list after a minor ankle sprain earlier this week, is now expected to participate in all drills as the coaching staff fine‑tunes its offensive game plan. The decision comes as Green Bay seeks to bolster a ground attack that has struggled to gain consistency this season, and it also underscores the team’s depth challenges on the defensive line with Parsons still out.

Jacobs, acquired in a trade last offseason, has been a bright spot for the Packers’ rushing corps, logging 62 carries for 280 yards and two touchdowns in his first five appearances. His ability to pick up blitzes and convert short-yardage situations has been especially valuable in a system that relies heavily on play‑action passing. Head coach Matt LaFleur praised the veteran’s work ethic during a press conference, noting that “Josh’s presence in practice pushes everyone to be better, and his experience is a real asset as we prepare for a tough divisional game.”

Parsons, the former Dallas Cowboys defensive end who signed a lucrative free‑agent deal with the Packers in the off‑season, suffered a Grade‑2 hamstring strain in the second half of last week’s practice. The injury has kept him out of the team’s weekly walkthrough and the subsequent film session. Defensive coordinator Joe Barry indicated that while the medical staff is optimistic about a return later in the season, the immediate focus will be on rotating the remaining pass‑rushers—primarily rookie edge rusher Jalen Williams and veteran edge Jake McFarland—to keep pressure on Detroit’s offensive line.

The upcoming matchup against the Lions carries added significance for both teams. Green Bay sits at 3‑3 on the season and needs a win to stay within striking distance of the NFC North lead, while Detroit, currently 2‑4, is fighting to avoid a prolonged losing streak. Analysts point to the Packers’ run game as a potential differentiator; a balanced attack could open up the play‑action passes that have been a staple of LaFleur’s offense. Conversely, the Lions’ defense has shown resilience against the run, ranking fourth in the league in yards allowed per carry, which could test Jacobs’ ability to find seams against a disciplined front seven.

The Packers’ front office appears confident that the team’s depth will absorb Parsons’ absence for now. Defensive line coach Mike Trgovac emphasized that “the unit is prepared to operate in a rotation that maximizes the health of our players while still delivering pressure.” Meanwhile, the offensive staff is expected to give Jacobs a larger share of snaps, potentially increasing his workload to 15‑20 carries per game. If Jacobs can capitalize on the added touches, Green Bay could establish a more credible threat on the ground and alleviate some of the burden on quarterback Jordan Love.

Looking ahead, the outcome of the Lions game will set the tone for the Packers’ mid‑season trajectory. A strong performance from Jacobs could solidify his role as a go‑to back and provide the offensive balance needed to compete with the division’s top teams. At the same time, the coaching staff will continue to monitor Parsons’ recovery, hoping to reintegrate the former All‑Pro into the rotation before the stretch run begins. The next few weeks will be pivotal in determining whether Green Bay can sustain its push for a playoff berth despite the lingering injuries on its defensive front.
